- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to prior period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +5% from prior), model often overshoots; cap next-period forecast at +3% above prior peak.
- If sentiment history shows strong bullish momentum (≥0.53 for 3+ consecutive days), model tends to overreact; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% to avoid overcorrection.
- When true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops 2–4% from recent peak), model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period if sentiment is neutral or bearish.
- For 30-day forecasts, if model’s first 3–5 days are significantly higher than true outcome, apply a “lag correction” — subtract 0.5–1.5% from forecast for days 1–3 if sentiment is weak or neutral.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.44/0.18), model often overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging 3–5 prior values before applying trend adjustment.
